components.name: Primary Button

narrative.overview:
The interface speaks the visual language a Spanish driver already reads at the edge of a Low Emission Zone: the blue information panel, the red-ringed ZBE disc, the round DGT environmental stickers and the EU number plate. Those artefacts appear only where they carry meaning (a rule, a label, a vehicle, an outcome); everything else is a quiet operating surface of flat white panels on a cool grey ground, separated by 1px rules.

Density is calm and projector-friendly: generous 1.5rem gutters, large type for figures, one accent colour doing most of the work. The system is restrained by design, chosen after a louder signage treatment proved "too much, not intuitive". It rejects the gradient hero over a row of shadowed emoji cards, and it rejects neon dark mode.

State is carried by colour families with fixed meaning: signage blue for action and the right to appeal, amber for money that is locked, green for money collected, grey for nothing happening, red only for the ZBE ring and for genuinely destructive acts.
keyCharacteristics: Flat white panels with 1px rules on a cool grey ground; no resting shadows.
Signage blue as the single action colour.
Real-world artefacts (road sign, ZBE disc, DGT stickers, EU plates) drawn in their true colours.
Overpass for everything, tabular figures for every amount and countdown.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Every actionable thing is Road Sign Blue or a neutral outline. No second accent is introduced for actions.

rules.name: The Appeal Is Not Danger Rule
rules.body: Appealing is a right, so the Appeal button and the Under-appeal status use blue (outline), never red.

rules.name: The Ring Is Reserved Rule
rules.body: ZBE Ring Red marks the zone sign and a locked-charge outcome only. Destructive actions use the separate Danger Red.

rules.name: The True Colours Rule
rules.body: DGT stickers, the ZBE disc and EU plates are drawn in their real-world colours and shapes, including the Eco sticker's hard green/blue split. They are depictions, not decoration.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every amount, countdown, charge number, plate and stat uses tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Weight Ladder Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from weight steps (650 labels and buttons, 750 titles and statuses, 800 headings and figures), not from colour or case. No uppercase labels.

rules.name: The Flat Panel Rule
rules.body: Panels, cards, tables and buttons carry no shadow. If something needs separation, use a 1px rule or a ground-to-panel step.

dos: Do keep panels flat: white, 1px Rule border, 12px radius, 1.5rem padding.
Do use Road Sign Blue for the one primary action on a screen, and for appeal actions as an outline.
Do show money state with the fixed pairs: amber for locked, green for collected, grey for cancelled or nothing charged.
Do draw labels as DGT stickers and vehicles as EU plates wherever a label or vehicle appears.
Do set every amount, plate, countdown and stat in tabular figures.
Do pair every status colour with an icon and a word.
Do keep a 44px minimum target for buttons and inputs.
donts: Don't add drop shadows to panels, cards or buttons; only toasts float.
Don't use ZBE Ring Red for buttons, text or fills; destructive actions use Danger Red.
Don't colour the Appeal action or Under-appeal status red.
Don't use decorative gradients; the Eco sticker's hard split is a depiction of the real sticker, not a gradient style.
Don't introduce a dark theme or neon accents; the scheme is light only.
Don't show a plate in clear text where this browser does not know it; show the hash.
